models._description: (extension) attribute tagged with an eCommerce comparison category

behavioral_notes.observation: Builds the comparison-table data structure that drives the /shop/compare page. It collects valid_product_template_attribute_line_ids.attribute_id across the products being compared, then nests an OrderedDict of product.attribute.category -> product.attribute -> {product: [product.template.attribute.value]}. Attributes with no category fall into an empty product.attribute.category bucket. Categories and attributes are .sorted() (category by sequence/id, see product_attribute_category._order). For no_variant attributes it falls back to attribute_line_ids.value_ids so all possible values are shown. This per-attribute, per-product alignment is exactly the row/column diffing of the comparison grid and is invisible to metadata.

http/public route that renders the comparison table. It does NOT read a server-side session list: it parses a `products` query-string CSV of product.product ids (e.g. /shop/compare?products=3,7,9), filters non-digits, and redirects to /shop when empty. It deliberately uses product.product.search([('id','in',ids)]) rather than browse() so public ACL read access is enforced per record, then renders website_sale_comparison.product_compare with the products (display_default_code=False). The set of ids to compare is supplied by the frontend (cookie) via the query string, not held in request.session.

jsonrpc/public endpoint returning per-product pricing/display data (display_name, website_url, image_1024 url, price, currency, strikethrough/compare_list_price) by calling product._get_combination_info_variant() for each id; used to hydrate the comparison bottom bar / rows. The grouping is data-modelled by the new product.attribute.category model (name, sequence index, attribute_ids one2many) plus the product.attribute.category_id ('eCommerce Category') extension, letting merchants regroup similar attributes into table sections. product.template.attribute.line._prepare_categories_for_display(_in_specs_table) reuses the same category grouping for the product-page spec table, filtering single custom-value lines.

behavioral_notes.element: compare list lives in a browser cookie + OWL/JS (gap #3), NOT in server session
behavioral_notes.observation: static/src/js/website_sale_comparison_utils.js stores compared product ids in a browser cookie `comparison_product_ids` (JSON array, MAX 4) with get/set/add/remove/clear helpers and an EventBus 'comparison_products_changed' event. The product_comparison public interaction wires .o_add_compare / .o_comparelist_remove clicks to add/remove (creating a variant via /sale/create_product_variant when needed), enforces max-4 and already-added warnings, mounts the ProductComparisonBottomBar OWL component, and on remove redirects to /shop/compare?products=<csv> (or /shop when empty). So the 'session-held' compare list is actually client cookie state threaded into the route via the query string, invisible to Python metadata.

side-effect: /shop/compare/get_product_data -> product._get_combination_info_variant for pricing/display in the compare bar

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: website_sale_comparison is a storefront merchandising/engagement add-on of the website_sale value network (auto_install=true on top of website_sale). It adds no chain document flow of its own: it neither transforms inputs nor confirms orders. Instead it enriches the shared eCommerce platform with a side-by-side attribute comparison capability that helps many anonymous/portal visitors self-select among catalog products (network logic of mediation over shared infrastructure, Stabell & Fjeldstad), inheriting website_sale's network classification. Its economic role is sell-side merchandising/conversion support on the online channel, hence APQC 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services (eCommerce merchandising). Activity is primary because it is customer-facing, revenue-channel functionality that directly supports the storefront purchase decision, not a back-office support function. strategy is null (human-supplied).

standard_capabilities: Public /shop/compare page rendering a side-by-side attribute comparison table
Attribute values aligned per attribute and grouped by configurable eCommerce attribute category
Add-to-compare / remove-from-compare buttons across shop and product pages
Client-side comparison list (cookie) capped at 4 products with de-duplication
Comparison bottom bar with live per-product price/display data (jsonrpc)
Reuse of attribute categories in the product-page specifications table
no_variant attributes show all possible values in the comparison
typical_fits: B2C catalogs where shoppers compare variants on technical attributes (electronics, appliances)
Merchants grouping many attributes into readable spec sections via product.attribute.category
Anonymous + logged-in shoppers comparing without an account
common_gaps: Server-side / persistent (cross-device) comparison lists - state is a browser cookie only
Comparing more than 4 products, or across different attribute taxonomies
Comparison analytics / conversion tracking (no server-side metrics)
Comparing non-attribute facts (price history, reviews, stock) beyond the provided price fields
Custom comparison-table layout beyond the supplied snippet/options

open_questions: Whether the comparison cookie is ever reconciled with a logged-in partner for cross-device persistence (appears purely client-side).
How _get_combination_info_variant resolves pricelist/discount context for anonymous vs portal users on the compare bar.
Whether merchants commonly curate product.attribute.category in practice, or attributes mostly fall into the uncategorized bucket.
